in_arabic.name: فَلَقاح
in_arabic.long_meaning: فَلَقاح هو المُسمى بالفَلاح، المُستَطيل، البَصير العَليم، من أسماء الله الحَسني، ويُعرف بالفَلاح في القرآن الكريم، في سورة الفَجر، الآية 1، وهو اسم مُستَمر في الإسلام، يُستخدم لِلقُرآن وَلِلنبي محمد، وسُمي به لِأنه رَآه فَلاجَه لِلهِ، أي رَآه مُستَطيلًا لا يَقدر العُلى وَلَا العِظم على مُجَدّده، وهو عَلى العُلى العَالِي، وهو البَصير العَليم مِثل رَبِّهِ

in_urdu.name: فَلَقاح

data.cultural_impact: The name Falaqah is a powerful reminder of the concept of seeking refuge or protection. In Islam, individuals are encouraged to seek refuge in Allah (God) for help, guidance, and protection from both worldly and spiritual harms. The name reflects the collective belief in seeking refuge and protection through prayer and faith.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Falaqah carries deep spiritual significance as it emphasizes the importance of seeking refuge in Allah (God). In the Islamic tradition, the final Sura (chapter) of the Quran is named "Al-Falaq," which begins with the statement, "Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the One God, from the evil I have done." This daily recitation of the sura is an essential part of the Islamic prayer ritual, symbolizing the reliance on the Divine for protection and assistance. Additionally, the concept of seeking refuge in Allah highlights the believer's submission and acknowledgment of God's authority and omnipotence.
